Otherwise keep the upper lip and chin smooth yellow. Dark skin shading, nose shadows and lip creases are not facial hair. The reference mascot's normal grey lip wedge or its shadow does not count as facial hair; do not merely recolor that lip and omit the moustache. Retain a narrow readable separation between the hair and mouth. Apply this only to genuinely visible source facial hair; clean-shaven sources retain the normal bare mascot mouth.
Retain the visible shape, symbol count and arrangement of source collar patches and existing decorations. Do not invent chest medallions. Any source note markings that are illegible remain indistinct texture; do not invent readable serial numbers, identification codes, words or labels.
Collar and anatomy: use a compact rounded mascot head seated close to broad shoulders, with a very short, wide neck transition. Widen and reshape the collar opening naturally around that base while keeping the original collar style, tabs, piping and badges. Collar front sits visibly in front of the lower neck; collar back sits behind it, with coherent perspective, contact shadow and fabric tension. No neck clipping through collar, pinched narrow ring, floating collar, broken seam or abrupt geometric junction. The creamy belly stays under opaque clothing; never add a cream/white bib on the neck. The head silhouette is nearly round or a SHORT egg shape. Its chin rests immediately above the garment collar, without copying the original human neck length. Preserve the shoulder position and crop by broadening the fitted garment; do not fill that space with a tall yellow column.
The garment meets the underside of a visibly rounded chin. There is no separate exposed vertical neck column between the head and collar, including bald and three-quarter-view portraits.
The lower head silhouette curves inward toward its base instead of continuing down as parallel straight yellow sides. Raise and broaden the original collar and shoulders to meet that curved chin; do not insert an extra yellow neck roll underneath it.
Keep the source's fastening state: a buttoned closed standing collar remains closed and buttoned, with both front ends meeting naturally at the center seam. Do not turn a closed military collar into a deep V-neck or unbuttoned shirt. Preserve open lapels/shirt collars only where the original is actually open.

Do not add such framing where absent. Polished painterly HOI4 finish, legible at the original in-game size. One source image to one asset. No comparison board, new text, label, watermark or extra figure.

Thick dark eyebrows, substantial short dark full beard AND upper-lip moustache, dark hair hidden under soft dark cylindrical military cap with a single gold star. Olive heavy jacket with broad open collar, cream/grey scarf around neck, diagonal brown strap. Preserve beard extent. Retain the source exact open/closed outfit layering and fastening, head angle and gaze, with a near-round yellow mascot head resting directly inside a widened tailored collar. No long yellow neck, cream neck bib or floating collar.
Final source-specific check: Retain the actual visible source facial hair with its correct extent and color; eyes, upper-lip moustache, source-shaped open or closed creature mouth, chin beard in that top-to-bottom order. No invented hair from shadows.
